sb_prompt: THE TOPIC IS CLOTHING.  PLEASE FIND OUT HOW THE OTHER CALLER TYPICALLY DRESSES FOR WORK.  HOW MUCH VARIATION IS THERE FROM DAY TO DAY?  HOW MUCH VARIATION IS THERE FROM SEASON TO SEASON?
turns: Yeah, it's kind of a uniform thing here, but I usually grab my own jeans and a nice blouse instead of the issued stuff if the floor isn't that dirty, though in the winter I'm stuck with those heavy, scratchy coats no matter what.

Oh wow, scratchy coats? That sounds awful, I don't think I could handle that; I'm lucky my scrubs are just cotton so I can swap them out if they get too hot, though I do need a jacket when it gets chilly walking between the chair and the sink.

Yeah, the fabric really gets under your skin, it's like sandpaper against your hips all shift, and honestly I've started wearing a thin thermal base layer just to keep the chafing down, though I don't have to wear it if the coat's thick enough.

Yeah, I hear you, but at least your coat is over everything, whereas mine gets soaked with spit and blood sometimes so I'm pretty much stuck in my own sweat no matter how many times I try to swap shirts.

Yeah, at least mine stays dry if I plan ahead, but man, the first week I was there I wore my own hoodie under the thing and it turned into a giant mess by noon, so now I just buy these cheap thermal shirts that wash well.
Yeah, that's the worst part about the cheap stuff, they pill up so fast you can't wear them twice.
Yeah, that's exactly why I switched to the ones with the cotton blend, even if they cost a buck fifty more at the store.
Yeah, the warmth is actually pretty nice once you get used to it, even if the quality is kinda hit or miss depending on the brand.
Yeah, honestly it's just a wash-and-wear thing, I'd rather not deal with dry cleaning when I'm running shifts.
Yeah, honestly I'd rather take a little extra time to dry clean than come to work feeling like I'm wearing a third skin, but I guess it's just the budget at the hospital these days.

Yeah, that's the thing with the factory budget, they don't even let you dry clean, so you just throw them in the wash and hope the stains don't set, which is why I try to spot-check before I clock out.

Yeah, I totally get the dry-cleaning headache, but at least your spots are just grease and oil, whereas my stuff gets blood and saliva that actually sets in after an hour if you don't treat it right away.
Yeah, that's the thing with blood, it sets so hard you basically have to hope you don't spill anything before you clock out.

Yeah, that's why I'm super careful before I clock out, I actually have this little stain remover pen in my coat pocket that I use on everything, but honestly it still leaves a weird ring sometimes if you wait even ten minutes.
That pen thing sounds like a lifesaver, but I guess I'm just lucky my stains are easier to scrub out if I get them out right away.
Yeah, I keep a little travel bottle of bleach in my desk drawer just in case, though I swear it smells like I've been mixing chemicals all day.
Yeah, I don't keep bleach in my pockets because it ruins the colors on my denim, so I just have to hope the pre-shift wipe-down was enough.
Yeah, I guess I'm just lucky my denim is bleach-proof, so at least I don't have to worry about turning my jeans pink like that one intern did last month.
Yeah, I actually had a kid try to wear their little pink dress under my uniform last year and ended up staining my best pair of jeans, so now I just check the pockets twice before I clock in.
Yeah, I keep telling that kid not to touch my stuff, but honestly he's never actually caused a stain on me, just a few wrinkles from being too excited.
Yeah, I think I finally convinced him that wrinkled clothes just look kind of lazy, even if they are freshly washed.
Yeah, maybe you're right, wrinkles are just ugly anyway, though I still tell my patients to smooth out their collars before they step into the chair.
Yeah, wrinkles are just ugly anyway, and honestly I'm starting to think you're right about that kid too, he just needs to learn to zip up his own jacket before he wanders off.
Yeah, maybe he just needs to learn that wrinkled clothes are just lazy anyway.
Yeah, I think I'm just going to give him a lint brush and tell him to shake it out before he goes.
Yeah, honestly he probably just needs to learn that wrinkles are just lazy anyway.
Yeah, that's probably the best way to handle it, just teach him to keep his stuff neat.
Yeah, maybe shaking it out won't hurt either.
Yeah, shaking it out probably works for you, but if he just folds it in half once before he leaves, that might fix it faster.
Yeah, folding it in half is probably the easiest thing to just do on the spot.
Yeah, folding it in half is definitely the quickest way to get it crisp without a steamer.
Yeah, honestly I just put mine in a tote and leave it on my desk till I leave work so I don't have to carry the crinkles around all day.
That tote trick sounds way better than folding stuff in my locker right before I clock out.
Yeah, that tote works great, it's way easier than trying to pack it all into my locker before I clock out.
Yeah, toss it in there and you're good to go.
Yeah, that tote works perfectly for that, I just leave it on the counter while I'm washing my hands so I can grab it right before I clock out.
Yeah, keeping it in the bag while you wash your hands is way smarter than trying to shove it in a locker full of tools.
Yeah, that's usually my thing too, just keep it easy until I clock out.
Yeah, I usually just toss my stuff in my locker and grab my own jacket on the way out, so I don't have to worry about wrinkling anything before I clock in.
Yeah, that's actually kind of my plan too, just keep it easy until I clock out.
